title: Instead of a step forward, it’s a step back
body: Marvel Unlimited has always been a subpar experience. So when it was announced that the largest digital comic book company in the world would be developing a new app I thought great, finally a good reader for marvel comics. Unfortunately what we got was almost the same as unlimited but with a few steps back. First of all, the way things are grouped in recent and downloads are a pain. It should be grouped by series but instead it’s all just single issues creating clutter. If you want to download things you need to hit 3 separate buttons for each and every issue. Have fun downloading an entire series that way. It wouldn’t be as big of an issue if they had collected editions. Why not? Another issue with downloads is that it doesn’t save your progress. If you read half an issue and then have to put it down because life, when you go back in it is right back to the cover. If you’re not connected to the internet and you try to continue series it tries to stream the next issue instead of just moving on to your next downloaded copy. Lastly for downloads, it doesn’t mark an issue as read after you’ve finished which makes it hard to keep track of your progress. Another issue is that in landscape mode there’s no option for reading 2 pages at a time side by side or with a fit to screen horizontal option. Also on my iPad, it gives you a 1/4” to 1/2” black border around each page, which effectively makes the page smaller than on Unlimited. Even little indie comic readers with tiny development teams give you options for these things. Another problem, if you’re reading comics from a reading guide and you hit continue after finishing an issue instead of reading the next issue in the order of the guide it instead reads the next issue of the series. Why even have guides at all if that’s how it works? Lastly you can’t make any kind of custom lists. Since the app doesn’t have omnibuses it would be nice to be able to collect all those issues yourself in the order they’re meant to be read in via custom lists, but there is no way to do that. Instead I guess I have to make a checklist on my phone to keep track of where I’m at. Overall I expected something better than Marvel Unlimited but instead what we got ended up being even worse than an already subpar app.

You still get to appreciate the full page’s composition—something you lose with smart panels—and you get the nice zoomed in view that you get with smart panels. Best of both worlds. Or if you wanted to read a bunch of series that came out at the same time you could sort by publication date. The only sorting options this app has is “A-Z” and “recently downloaded” which puts your newest downloads at the top. So if you want to make a reading list, you have to download them in reverse order. In general the downloads page is a pain— there’s no option button for each comic and they don’t mark them as read when you finish an issue. There are some marked improvements from unlimited: being able to delete multiple comics at once is very welcome. And the search function already seems to be miles ahead of what unlimited has. It also seems to load much faster than unlimited did. I’m hoping that in the coming months some of these old functionalities will be incorporated into the webtoons platform.

title: Screenshots kick you out, making Marvel Comics a lonely experience.
body: I’m very disappointed that I can’t take any screenshots of my favorite panels. One of the funnest parts of reading comics books on the previous Marvel App (Marvel Unlimited) is finding funny panels, or epic panels and then sending them to my friends and encouraging them to go and read the issue as well. Reading comics digitally was fun because I could quickly text my buddies and say “woah! Check this out!” And then they’d ask which comic it was, and who the artist was, and I’d go look it up and share that with them. Sadly now reading Spider-Man will now be an isolated experience for me. I really wish I’d caught myself up to present day before MU was shut down. If you guys are dead set on not allowing screenshots, please consider at least letting us screenshot individual panels, or having a limited number per day so we can encourage others to pick up a copy as well.

title: Fixes that Need to Be Made!
body: I was extremely excited for the release of this app because I thought that it would be a direct upgrade from Unlimited. While I appreciate how responsive this new app is and the Ultimate option to get new comics sooner, many things are worse in the new version that need to be addressed quickly for all of your readers: 1. Absolute first priority should be to remove the screenshot limitations and allow users to share the world of Marvel comics with others online 2. Please also allow us to remove series from continue reading and download issues from the home page!! 3. Issues need to be resized to fit phone and tablet screens without a visible black bar at the top or bottom. It just looks a lot worse than Unlimited which had no problem with this. I've heard iPhone Duo users are also having issues with this, so please give them an optimized experience! 4. Make the app or another way to read Marvel comics and have past purchases available in Japan and Korea 5. Regional pricing for regions with lower average income needs to be a thing to make it actually affordable 6. Filters (date range, creator, character, read/unread, etc.) like those on Unlimited have to be added to the series, creator, and character pages and there needs to be a search bar in the creator filter to make it actually usable 7. Mature-rated series like MAX and Red Band HAVE to be added to the library! It's getting ridiculous how these are literally impossible to read anywhere legally I believe that's everything I have experienced and I've seen others address online that would go a long way toward making this app the definitive premier location for Marvel Comics

It should scale to fit the screen side to side instead of trying to show a full page with most of the screen black on the sides. Would be a much higher rating with this feature.

title: Why’d they change so much

We can’t mark issues as read or remove them from the “Continue Reading” bar unless we fully open that series’ page. They also added a screenshot blocker, sharing screenshots from comics is one of the biggest way books generate hype and publicity… to remove that makes zero sense.

title: Please Bring Back the Sorting and Filtering Options!
body: As someone who has only recently gotten into reading comics, my biggest frustration with the new Marvel Comics app is the lack of sorting and filtering options that are available in the Marvel Unlimited app. I’m currently reading through all of Spider-Man’s comic appearances in publication order. Since characters often appear across multiple comic series at the same time, being able to easily find their next appearance is incredibly helpful. Marvel Unlimited allows you to filter out issues you’ve already read, making it easy to pick up where you left off. The new Marvel Comics app, however, only lets you sort a character’s appearances by “Newest” or “Oldest.” This means having to endlessly scroll through hundreds or even thousands of issues just to find the next unread appearance. For newer comic readers trying to explore decades of Marvel history, these sorting and filtering features are incredibly valuable. Marvel Unlimited also offers additional filtering options and the ability to switch between grid and list views, neither of which is available on the new app’s character pages. I was excited about the promised new features, but I really hoped they wouldn’t come at the expense of essential features that Marvel Unlimited already offers. Please bring these sorting and filtering options to the new Marvel Comics app, especially the ability to hide already-read issues! The new app should make exploring Marvel’s history easier, not harder.

I just wish that there would be an option to sync my digital library to Apple Books if not have the one-for-one interface experience. If this can be addressed immediately, then the Marvel Comics app would live up to the Marvel Unlimited legacy. One could say the app could be… Superior 😉. But so far the lack of page-turning has brought my rating to something average. Let’s get it done, you guys!

title: I expected more…
body: I was always disappointed with the Marvel Unlimited app and this is basically the exact same thing. Here are my suggestions: 1. We need custom folders. DC’s app blows this one away just because of that feature. Why can’t I make my own folders and name them what I want to organize my reading list the way I want to? 2. Now when you browse series and choose to list them by the newest first it also alphabetizes them. Why? I want to see the newest series by date not the newest Amazing Spider-Man first followed by the newest Black Panther etc. I really hope you take suggestions to heart as there is no reason this should not have basic features like the DC app has. Improve it and I will also improve my score.

title: A good start, but needs improvement
body: Things look pretty good so far, but the inability to remove things from my waiting list is a huge miss. Fix that problem and I’ll update my review.

title: Solid Start, But Still Missing Essential Tools
body: Long-time Marvel Unlimited subscriber with a large library. The new app has promise, but it dropped features serious readers rely on. Top priorities: 1. Library filtering. Unlimited could filter by read/unread, publication date, character, creator, series, and owned titles. The new Series/Issues/Reading Guides/Redeemed views are not a substitute. In a library of thousands of issues, read/unread and date filters are essential. 2. Remove from Continue Reading. Without it, the row fills with sampled or abandoned titles. 3. Saving a series should save all its issues, including future releases. Saving each issue one by one is tedious. A setting or "Save all" button would also work. Also missing: sorting by publication date (needed to read a run in order) and page numbers. The iPad experience also needs work; it should be the best way to read comics, and it isn't yet. Library organization: let users build their own structure, separate from Marvel's metadata. Series and character views can't capture creative runs, reading eras, or events that span multiple titles. Nested folders or bookshelves would let readers group comics the way they actually read them, e.g., an X-Men folder containing Claremont Era, Morrison Era, and Krakoan Age. User-created tags would be a reasonable alternative. Other ideas to surpass Unlimited: - More filter/sort options: digital vs. print release date, volume/issue/legacy number, facsimile editions, format, and era - Flag issues owned in print - Variant cover browsing If you have a large library, please request these too. The more users ask, the more likely they get prioritized.

title: Decent experience. Needs more filtering for your stuff.
body: This app is a decent experience. It obviously needs more filtering features for your own items and those lists. I need to be able to only see things I’m actively reading or going to read. Some way to sort by title or recently opened or series etc. Some way to make lists of things. Just a better management approach for my stuff.

title: Fine for a rollout, but more features are still needed
body: Look, it gets the job done. You want to read a comic? You can read that comic (as long as it was already on Marvel Unlimited). But there are a number of features from MU currently missing that I hope can be implemented in future releases. To wit: * Syncing of progress in a download with server-side data. If I finish or read part of a downloaded comic, that progress isn’t reflected in the server-side information about my reading. Ex: I recently read a three-issue miniseries I had downloaded. But when I went to check its status on the Marvel Comics App, none of the issues were marked read. * The ability to sort downloads in multiple ways. Here’s my use case: I download a bunch of comics across series according to a reading order. I then want to read them in that order. Alphabetical sorting is subpar, and the current download order puts the most recently downloaded comics at the top. I want to have them at the option to have to oldest downloaded comics at the top so I don’t have to scroll to the bottom of the page to read the comics in the order I downloaded them. There are probably also people who would like to be able to sort their downloads by release date. * More filtering on the series page. When I pull up a series, I want to be able to filter out the issues I’ve already read. Right now my options are to either click the “start reading” button which puts me in the most recent unread comic or to scroll down to find it, if I want to see the comic (say for downloading) but not read it right away. There were a number of other filters that could be applied in MU (like creators and dates), that should also be ported over. * Can we get rid of the 30-day download limit? While I probably read the comics I download within 30 days, I’ve never kept track. This feels like it’s adding an unnecessary limit for no real purpose, since once a download expires I can just redownload it if I need to.

title: Needs some catching up to Unlimited
body: As others have mentioned, it would be very nice to allow us the option to remove comics from the continue reading section. I was also bombarded with piles and piles of comics from series I've since long abandoned and had to go to my reading history to get rid of them. The transitions between panels in panel-to-panel mode is also a lot slower and less smooth than it was on Unlimited. I hope the quality of panel-to-panel will be restored to that of Unlimited's. It would also be nice to see the page number #/# or process bar in the panel-to-panel overview heading. The one you tap once to bring it up while you're reading. It's nice that the screenshot has been restored immediately so thank you to the team for taking that feedback to heart.

title: Decent

They’re comic panels, screenshots are just cause we like the actual page, not cause we’re mass distributing. Most pointless overreach possible, remove that asap.

You can manually pinch-to-zoom to push the page to the very edge, but as soon as you go to the next page it’s cropped in again. Marvel Unlimited used every bit of the screen.

The user interface is updated, as one would expect, but I would be reluctant to call it better. I read on my phone, and the buttons register clicks much easier now. But I prefer Unlimited's approach to reading actual issues. Maybe I'm not explaining this well, but anyone who used the Marvel Unlimited app will notice some minor differences. I do not think this app is yet better than Marvel Unlimited. As of right now, it's just different, and we will see if any of the small flaws get updated out. If you are simply looking fot a collection of nearly all of Marvel's issues, you will likely find this app more than sufficient.

title: Good Start - Missing personal favorite features
body: The launch of the new app has been smooth. I’d just like to highlight a few key features I used frequently in Marvel Unlimited that seem to be missing from this current version. 1. My prefer reading method is on iPad in landscape mode. In the old app, the landscape mode immediately fit to the screen whereas now you have to manually resize each page. Since this is a feature I use with every comic I would prefer an update to fix this in the very near future. 2. In the old app, I used reading guides extensively and upon finishing a comic you would be prompted with either continuing your next read from the guide or from the next issue from the series. There is currently no option to continue reading from the guide. This is an annoyance but I don’t doubt it will be resolved later. These next items are not immediate needs but I would find them helpful if included. 3. Currently when you are utilizing the Smart Panel feature and try to open the page options the page number does not appear. You have to disable Smart Panel, review the page number, and then re-enable Smart Panel to go back to reading. Please allow the page number to appear when using the Smart Panel feature. 4. Infinite scrolling - not a need but a nice to have. 5. I’ve seen issues with people screenshotting and be given warnings. I’d prefer to allow users to screenshot, otherwise, please clearly explain the intended functionality. I’d hate to accidentally press the screenshot button on my phone or iPad and be banned from the service. Overall, the app is fine and I’m looking forward to future updates that can bring this to a five star rating.

This leads to the phone dimming pretty quickly and needing to always touch the page to undim. I felt the Unlimited app did a good job of helping you find new content. This new app at least initially I feel is a step behind in content discovery. Not being tied to the Disney ecosystem anymore is also a bit strange. Don’t love it, but don’t hate it. Hope the devs can get some quick updates in before the new year.

Right now it includes EVERY series I’ve ever looked at a single issue of. Marking the issues as “unread” doesn’t take it out. The only way I can find to do it is to mark every issue in the series as “read” which is not convenient if it’s a series with hundreds of issues. I’m hoping this is addressed soon in an update.

title: Not better/Not Worse
body: I haven’t spent an extensive amount of time on this app but the time spent was enjoyable and not amazing or spectacular or anything like that. The homepage is surprisingly similar to unlimited homepage, which in retrospect does help me understand everything a lot better. The upcoming segment of the app is a welcome addition but it does kinda feel like it’s pushing the upgraded tier a bit more than the original did. Also for some reason they still have the ultimate spider-man and it’s infinite comics version on one tab which is odd to me. Also a person thing for me, I want a large reading guide that just has every appearance available for “comic historian” like me (I’m not really I’m lying) so I can read it start to finish, I know completely selfish but I gotta ask if I actually want it. (I’ve been trying to read spider-man stuff but everytime I finish an issue I gotta do all this research on what to read next, should just be one big reading guide for people like me) anyway not a bad app, will love to see how much it’s supported and updated.

title: So far not bad :)
body: The app runs faster compared to Marvel Unlimited and the layout is much cleaner! I also love more clear info for an individual issue. However, there are a couple issues I’ve noticed just from the 1st day so far: 1. Screenshotting is disabled (sort of). Very disappointing and this is MY BIGGEST COMPLAINT. I get the intention is to dissuade piracy but this will cause people to pirate anyways. I loved being able to share my favorite panels with friends and save my favorite panels for memories. Please allow screenshotting again! 2. Lack of personalized lists. You cant create your own lists of comics you like 3. Reading orders are a little messy. Some reading guides go in publication order which messes with the chronology of an event. Just give the option for actual chronological order instead and I think that will be fine. 4. Continue reading feature when you want to go back or forward to a previous issue is oddly lacking compared to marvel unlimited. Overall not a bad start and hopefully my complaints are answered!

title: UPDATE: they backed off on the screenshot ban. Star rating updated accordingly.
body: This app is a lot smoother and faster than Marvel Unlimited. Search is MUCH better. My Marvel Unlimited history seems to have imported with no problems. Downloading multiple comics is more of a chore, but being able to select multiple items to delete them is a godsend. I noticed that downloads have a one-month time limit, but that won’t ever be a problem. But what is a problem is that I can take screenshots in the app, but it flashes an alert and kicks me out of the issue every time I do. That knocks this app down two full stars for me. Please reconsider this decision. I’m sure it’s to prevent piracy, but (a) it’s not going to work and (b) it’s pretty rotten to treat the 99.9% of your paying subscribers who aren’t stealing your comics like criminals by enabling this feature. There are many legitimate reasons to take screenshots of comics: for journalistic purposes, to share on social media, to drop into YouTube videos, etc. We are paying for this app as an ALTERNATIVE to pirating comics. Don’t treat us like the pirates.

title: So cool, especially on the duo

title: One big issue already
body: Us phone readers NEED the ability to “fill to screen” in horizontal. That is the only way I can read comfortably. I had hoped this app would be an improvement from Marvel Unlimited but with that feature gone idk if I can see myself sticking around much longer. My eyes hurt, and that’s not worth my money.

title: The best
body: I’ve used unlimited since it came out. This is a huge step up. Love the new search features. Comics all look great. Get it!

title: Perfect!
body: I love this app so far the only thing it needs that’s probably already getting worked on is optimization for IPhone Duo. Keep up the good work!

title: I love it
body: So far it is really good, but I do think that Max should be added even if it is behind the higher tier subscription. It is also difficult to tell what issues I have read and which ones I haven’t when I view series. Besides those 2 things it is perfect.

title: Finally a usable Marvel Comics app
body: This new Marvel Comic app is so much more user-friendly than the horrible old app. This new one is comparable to DC Infinite. I’m so happy I can finally enjoy Marvel again.

title: Much more organized and cool
body: I was a fan of marvel unlimited and happy to say this app is much easier to use than it’s predecessor. I would say I need one feature, when looking into a character and all of their issues we can only change the order from oldest to newest. We need a feature to be able to filter out what was read and not read, and maybe a select all or multiple to click what you read
